name: traceroute
purpose: Observe responding hops toward a destination.
caution: Routers may filter probes; missing hops and return paths do not establish forwarding failure.

name: tracert
purpose: Trace the route using ICMP probes.
caution: Asterisks mean no timely reply to that probe, not necessarily packet loss for application traffic.

name: nmap
purpose: Inventory selected reachable ports on an authorized host.
caution: Run only within authorized scope. Service on a port cannot be identified conclusively by port number alone.

name: netstat
caution: Example is Windows. Elevated access may be required to identify processes; output can reveal sensitive internal endpoints.

name: ip address
purpose: Inspect configured interface addresses and link state.
caution: Reading configuration does not prove off-link connectivity or DNS functionality.

name: ip route
purpose: Inspect routing decisions and installed routes.
syntax: ip route show | ip route get address
caution: Policy routing, namespaces, and VRFs can change the effective route.

name: ip neighbor
purpose: Inspect IPv4 ARP and IPv6 neighbor cache entries.
caution: A stale neighbor entry is not necessarily a fault; the kernel revalidates reachability when needed.

name: ifconfig
purpose: Inspect interface addressing on systems that provide net-tools.
caution: On modern Linux, use ip for complete contemporary interface configuration.

name: dig
purpose: Query a specific DNS record and inspect the response.
caution: Answers can differ by resolver, cache, location, and policy; inspect status and TTL as well as address values.

name: dig -x
purpose: Perform a PTR lookup for an IP address.
caution: A PTR record is administrative DNS data and does not verify ownership or service identity.

name: nslookup
purpose: Query a DNS server interactively or for a selected record type.
caution: A default resolver may apply split DNS; record the resolver when comparing answers.

name: tcpdump
purpose: Inspect a bounded packet capture matching a filter.
caution: Captures can contain sensitive data and require authorization and privileges. Interface names vary.

name: ss
purpose: Inspect sockets and their connection state.
caution: Listening on 0.0.0.0 or :: has broader exposure than a loopback-only bind; verify firewall policy too.

name: curl
purpose: Inspect an HTTP response header set.
caution: HEAD responses can differ from GET; certificate and redirect behavior should be inspected intentionally.

name: ipconfig
purpose: Inspect Windows interface, DHCP, and resolver settings.
caution: Output contains hostnames and adapter details; redact before sharing publicly.
